headline: Georgia regulators have fined two companies a combined 42,500 dollars for starting to build a gas-fired power plant for a data center without the required permits.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 6: new AJC report; the exact date of the fines is not stated in the readable text.
importance_line: Residents near Covington get stricter pollution limits on a fast-built gas plant, but the project continues despite the violation.
summary: The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports that VoltaGrid and Serverfarm agreed to pay 11,500 and 31,000 dollars after Georgia's Environmental Protection Division found them assembling dozens of gas-powered generators at a site in Covington, about 40 miles east of Atlanta, without the required permits. The companies may keep building the plant and data center under stricter emissions limits, and the violation notices came a day after the AJC reported on the missing permits.
